chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him), 'Dirhams come to me with some surplus (remainder), so we buy it with the money (coins).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible, but look at the surplus between the two, weigh the brass (or base metal) and weigh the surplus, so place it with the good dirhams, and take weight by weight.'
ai.seo_question: How to handle surplus weight when exchanging mixed silver dirhams according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of *bay' al-darāhim* (silver coin exchange) by distinguishing between the intrinsic value of the silver and the extrinsic weight of base metals in mixed currency. The Imam instructs that the surplus (debased portion) must be weighed separately and exchanged *mithlan bi-mithl* (equal weight for equal weight) with good dirhams, ensuring the transaction adheres to the prohibition of *riba* (usury) in currency exchange. This method preserves the integrity of the silver standard while allowing practical use of debased coins in daily commerce.
